note: Placeholder values. Review with a flight surgeon and NASA-STD-3001 before real use.

dose.watch: Your mission dose is above half of the 600 mSv NASA career limit (earlier flights also count). Review shelter time and planned activities with your flight surgeon.
dose.alert: Your dose is above 80% of the 600 mSv career limit. Contact your flight surgeon now to review your radiation plan.

sleep.watch: Keep a fixed sleep window, dim lights an hour before, and avoid caffeine and hard exercise late in the day. If sleep stays low for 3 more days, send a report to the flight surgeon.
sleep.alert: Very short sleep affects judgment and safety. Rest before any critical task if you can, tell the crew, and contact your flight surgeon.

mood.watch: Talk with the crew or call home, take a short break, and try slow breathing. If low mood continues for several days, contact your flight surgeon.
mood.alert: Contact your flight surgeon or behavioral health support today.

heart.watch: Rest, drink water, avoid caffeine and re-check when calm. If it stays raised for 3 days, send a report. Chest pain, fainting or shortness of breath: contact your flight surgeon now.

bp.watch: Sit quietly for 5 minutes and measure again. Check fluids and salt intake. If it is still outside range, send a report. Severe headache, chest pain or fainting: contact your flight surgeon now.

temp.watch: Measure again after 15 minutes, drink fluids and rest. Report it if it persists or comes with other symptoms.
temp.alert: Contact your flight surgeon now. Consider limiting close contact with crewmates until you hear back.

glucose.watch: Measure again and note when you last ate. If it is out of range twice, send a report.

tension.watch: Take a short break or do a shared activity. If tension continues, tell the flight surgeon or behavioral health support.

meals.watch: Try small, regular meals and extra fluids. Low appetite for several days reduces energy, muscle and bone health, so tell the flight surgeon if it continues.

exercise.watch: Add a short session today. Resistive and cardio exercise help protect muscles and bones in microgravity.

symptoms.watch: Note when each symptom started and how strong it is, and add details to the report note. Report eye or vision changes even if mild.
symptoms.alert: Nausea or vomiting, especially after a solar event: contact your flight surgeon now.
